title: How Technology Is Transforming Small Businesses
author: Maria Santos
excerpt: Discover how accessible digital tools are leveling the playing field for small entrepreneurs to compete with large corporations.
content:
The current landscape

It has never been easier for a small business to access tools that were once exclusive to large corporations. Management platforms, marketing automation and data analysis are now within reach of any entrepreneur.

Tools that make a difference

Among the key technologies positively impacting small businesses are CRM systems, e-commerce platforms and digital payment solutions.

How to get started

The first step is to map your business processes and identify where technology can automate repetitive tasks. This frees up time for you to focus on what really matters: growth.

title: 5 Tips to Code Better and Be More Productive
author: Carlos Lima
excerpt: Check out our essential tips to improve your productivity as a developer and write quality code.
content:
1. Write clean code

Readable code is code you can maintain six months from now. Use descriptive names, small functions and comments when necessary.

2. Do code reviews

Reviewing a colleague's code improves both the final product and your own learning. Build a culture of constructive feedback.

3. Test your code

Automated tests prevent regressions and give you confidence to refactor. Start with unit tests and expand to integration tests.

4. Use version control

Git is not optional. Learn the workflow with branches, atomic commits and descriptive messages.

5. Invest in continuous learning

Technology evolves fast. Set aside weekly time to study new tools, read documentation and follow the community.
seoTitle: 5 Tips to Code Better — Practical Guide
seoDescription: Essential tips to improve your productivity as a developer and write quality code.

title: Managing Remote Teams: The Complete Guide for 2026
author: Ana Oliveira
excerpt: Remote work is here to stay. Learn how to structure processes, tools and culture so your distributed team is highly productive.
content:
Why remote management requires a different approach

In-person teams benefit from informal communication and shared context. In remote work, everything needs to be explicit, documented and asynchronous by default.

Pillars of an effective remote team

The three pillars are: clear communication, autonomy with accountability, and the right tools. None replaces the other two.

Recommended tools

For asynchronous communication, Notion and Linear. For video calls, any solution works — what matters is having well-defined rituals. For task management, use what the team already knows.

Building culture remotely

Culture is not what's in the handbook. It's what happens when no one is watching. Celebrate wins, give fast feedback and create spaces for informal conversations.
seoDescription: How to structure processes, tools and culture so your remote team is highly productive.

title: Cash Flow: Why It Is More Important Than Profit
author: Roberto Campos
excerpt: Profitable businesses fail every year due to cash flow problems. Understand the difference between profit and cash and learn to monitor your financial health.
content:
The profit-without-cash paradox

It is possible to have a profitable business on paper and not have money to pay suppliers. This happens when sales are on credit and costs are paid upfront.

How to calculate your cash flow

Sum all projected inflows for the period and subtract all outflows. A negative cash flow is not necessarily bad — the problem is when it comes as a surprise.

Practical tips

Keep a reserve equivalent to three months of fixed expenses. Encourage early payments with discounts. Negotiate longer terms with suppliers.
seoTitle: Cash Flow: Why It Is More Important Than Profit

title: How to Build an Onboarding Process That Retains Talent
author: Ana Oliveira
excerpt: The first 90 days of an employee determine whether they stay or leave. See how to create a structured and human integration process.
content:
Why onboarding matters

Companies with well-structured onboarding processes have 82% higher retention in the first year. An employee who leaves in the first six months costs an average of 50% of their annual salary.

The three stages of onboarding

Pre-onboarding (before the first day), integration (first two weeks) and initial development (up to 90 days). Each stage has distinct objectives.

Elements of effective onboarding

Buddy program, first-task checklist, frequent feedback meetings and clarity on expectations. Simple as that — what's lacking is consistent execution.
